angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,931,959 km at 30.90 pc = 0.84 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 56537: the Hipparcos parallax the radius was computed with (van Leeuwen 2007), 32.36 +/- 0.22 mas, inverted (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 30.902 +/- 0.21 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 32.6068 +/- 0.2062 mas (same row, RUWE 1.73), 158.1 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 2.777 +/- 0.047 solar radii from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 56537: radius in solar radii, from the limb-darkened angular diameter 0.835 +/- 0.013 mas (CHARA) and the Hipparcos parallax, 2.777 +/- 0.047 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101): 1,931,959 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 2.111 +/- 0.01 solar masses from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 56537: mass in solar masses, from Yonsei-Yale isochrones at the measured radius and temperature (a model value), 2.111 +/- 0.01 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 8007 +/- 77 K from Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 56537: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 8007 +/- 77 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Boyajian et al. (2012), ApJ 746, 101, HD 56537: effective temperature in K, from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux, 8007 +/- 77 (https://doi.org/10.1088/0004-637X/746/1/101)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/lambda-geminorum.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 3.875, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Kharitonov, Tereshchenko & Knyazeva (1988), Spectrophotometric Catalogue of Stars (Alma-Ata), record 473) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
